tasks.title: A hub eavesdrops, a switch does not
tasks.statement: Three computers are connected to a hub. PC 1 and PC 2 talk to each other, while PC 3 sees every one of their frames: the hub repeats everything to all ports. Replace the hub with a switch: delete the three cables (select a cable on the diagram and click “Delete cable”) and connect the computers to the switch. Then click ▶ on the eavesdropping goal and make sure the frame does not reach PC 3.
tasks.hint: Select the cable line with a click, then “Delete cable”. For a new connection use the “Cable” mode: click a PC and then the switch. After the first exchange the switch knows which port PC 1 and PC 2 are behind.

spec_text./goals/1/text: PC 3 is on the network too: it pings PC 1
spec_text./goals/2/text: Frames between PC 1 and PC 2 do not reach PC 3

tasks.title: Remove the loop
tasks.statement: Three switches are connected in a ring. A broadcast frame (and an ARP request is exactly that) will circle the ring forever: a storm. Click ▶ on the goal and look at the log: a switch notes that the frame has already passed through it. Break the ring so that a tree remains but the network stays connected. This is what the STP protocol does automatically by blocking an extra port.
tasks.hint: Select any cable between switches and delete it. The three switches will remain connected in a chain, and that is enough.

spec_text./goals/1/text: The network has no loop (frames do not go in circles)

tasks.title: Two virtual networks on one switch
tasks.statement: Accounting (PC 1, PC 2) and development (PC 3, PC 4) are plugged into the same switch and can currently see each other. Split them into two VLANs: accounting is VLAN 10, development is VLAN 20. Communication within a department must remain, and between departments it must be cut. The VLAN number is set per port in the switch card.
tasks.hint: On the switch: PC 1 is port p1, PC 2 is p2, PC 3 is p3, PC 4 is p4. Set VLAN 10 on p1 and p2, VLAN 20 on p3 and p4. Or in the terminal: `port p1 vlan 10`.

tasks.title: A trunk between switches
tasks.statement: The departments sit on two floors, and each floor has its own switch. Accounting: PC 1 (first floor) and PC 3 (second floor), development: PC 2 and PC 4. Configure VLAN 10 and 20 on the access ports and turn port p8 on each switch into a trunk, so that both VLANs travel over one cable with tags. PCs of the same department must see each other across floors, and other departments must not.
tasks.hint: Access ports: p1 is VLAN 10, p2 is VLAN 20 on both switches. Port p8 of each switch is “trunk”. Without a trunk the tags will not pass and PC 1 will not reach PC 3.
